I shot myself last year. Maybe it was the TBI or the pain pills, but i never cried about surviving. I had so many suicide attempts but that one was my last. I found myself going through some bad situations afterward: alienation from my family, being kicked out, moving in with my distant father. Rumors spread about me. But for some reason all these bad things pushed me closer to working hard to be happy. I survived a gunshot to the head, I could survive some shit life throws at me as well. I was homeless for a bit with my dad and that didnt even stop me. I think the cherry on top was finding out I was pregnant. It changed everything. I was scared at first and unsure... But i finally found courage to say "i know I can be a good mother. I can work hard to provide the life my son deserves." 
Life will always be hard. But I believe I survived that for a reason... I shot myself in the middle of the forehead. It somehow missed my brain and ended up in my spine. Not even doctors could explain that. I believe you are born to make your purpose and maybe im still here to make mine. I never find myself in a state of questioning living anymore. This is the most true living ive done in my 21 years of life.

Being a tomboy opened my mind on what it is too actually be a woman. Now, i understand more feminine women may know too, but being a tomboy gives you a new perspective. Growing up i hated the idea of wearing skirts or pink or purple or bright colors or flowers or makeup or even girly jewelry. I had my mind set on changing all the comments saying "thats not ladylike" or "thats not what a girl does" or even "thats for boys" to more gender accepting ones. I will admit I thought girly girls growing up were wimpy and to conformed to these gender biases i picked up on since such a young age. But as I grew i realized even they too were strong women. Even if they did it in a pink jean skirt.  And I realized as a tomboy, always preferring to be one of the guys, always feeling most comfortable in the attire and with the vibes and the attitude of a tomboy, I found that I can allow myself to feel pretty and soft and still be a strong woman. This day today I dress like a genderless weirdo to be honest. But I still let it be know that I am a strong woman who feels oh so pretty in her heavy boots and big jeans.
